ideas.name: Token-unlock dilution short, beta-hedged
ideas.rule: For each large scheduled unlock (cliff or team/investor tranche with unlocked amount >= 2-3% of circulating supply, token has a Kraken Futures PF_ perp), short the token perp at T-14 days and cover at T+3 days, with the notional hedged by a long BTC perp (beta from 90-day rolling regression). Equal-weight, max 5 concurrent positions, 1-2x gross leverage, 8% hard stop on the hedged leg.
ideas.rationale: Who pays: holders and late buyers who ignore a public supply schedule; the insiders/VC receiving tokens are price-insensitive sellers and market makers hedge ahead of the delivery, so the price is pushed down before and around the date. It persists because shorting small caps is capacity-limited and costly (borrow/funding, thin books), and many retail buyers do not track unlock calendars. Risk: partly priced in (declines begin about a month ahead), and short squeezes on small caps.
ideas.evidence: Keyrock, 16,000+ unlocks: ~90% followed by declines, larger unlocks give sharper drops, impact starts ~30 days before, team unlocks worst (https://keyrock.com/from-locked-to-liquidity-what-16000-token-unlocks-teach-us/ ; coverage https://beincrypto.com/keyrock-research-token-unlocks/). A practitioner event study (36-38 large events) found beta-adjusted CAR[-30,+30] of -15.05%, bootstrap 95% CI [-24.8%, -5.5%], but a systematic short on 59 Binance perps with dilution >5% was not robust after costs (found via search, personal write-up, not peer-reviewed). Analogue: IPO lock-up expiry literature in equities. Industry sources have undisclosed methods and likely survivorship bias (dead tokens).
ideas.data: Prices: Kraken Futures charts API (verified 200: https://futures.kraken.com/api/charts/v1/trade/PF_XBTUSD/1h?from=..&to=..) and Kraken instruments list (verified, has openingDate), Binance data.binance.vision archives (verified). Unlock schedules are the weak point: DefiLlama /emissions returns 402 (paid) and CoinGecko new-coins endpoint needs a key. Free route: scrape the public Tokenomist/TokenUnlocks and CoinMarketCal pages, or reconstruct from on-chain vesting contracts/project docs for the ~30-50 tokens that have Kraken perps. Realistic history: 2022-2026, probably 100-200 events after filtering to Kraken-listed perps. Collection effort is about a day, tight.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures perpetuals (short alt perp + long PF_XBTUSD hedge). Paper-only feasible; cost about 0.05% taker per side plus slippage (assume 0.10-0.20% on small caps) plus funding (shorts usually receive funding in bull regimes, pay in bear).
ideas.test: Design period 2022-01 to 2025-06: event study of beta-adjusted returns by window, pick only ONE entry/exit pair and ONE size threshold from 4 candidates (cap trials at ~10, count them). Sealed control: 2025-07 to 2026-11 events, never touched, plus a placebo of random dates on the same tokens. Pass if: control net-of-cost mean per event > +1.5% hedged, hit rate > 55%, at least 40 control events, the result survives dropping the top 3 events and doubling costs, and placebo shows nothing. Fail otherwise.
ideas.expected: Honest: +3% to +8% per year on EUR 1,000 net of costs if the effect is real (event count is low, position sizes small); a real chance of zero because the effect is likely partly arbitraged and the practitioner test failed after costs. Drawdown 8-15% (squeeze risk on thin alts, imperfect BTC hedge).

ideas.name: Post-listing fade on newly listed perps / announced tokens
ideas.rule: Whenever a new token appears (Kraken spot or Kraken Futures new PF_ perp, or a Binance/Coinbase listing announcement), do NOT chase the announcement pop. Enter a short on the Kraken perp (when one exists) at listing day close+1h (or at day+1 open for tokens without a perp, using the spot-list-based sim only for the paper-test), hold 7 days, exit by time stop or +15% stop. Equal weight 5% notional per trade, max 4 open.
ideas.rationale: Who pays: retail momentum buyers who buy after the announcement and listing-day hype; the pre-announcement insiders and early holders sell into that liquidity. IPO-style long-run underperformance (Ritter) and sell-the-news dynamics. It persists as long as new listings attract attention-driven flows and shorting at the time of listing is operationally hard, so arbitrageurs are limited. Risk: very high squeeze/gap risk, perps for new tokens often listed late on Kraken (the effect may already be spent).
ideas.evidence: Avarikioti & Christin (Coinbase vs Binance listings): mean day-of announcement returns of +32.8% (Coinbase) and +22.7% (Binance), i.e. the pop exists, the question is what follows (https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol354-aft2025/html/LIPIcs.AFT.2025.11/LIPIcs.AFT.2025.11.html). An Erasmus thesis on cross-listing across 11 exchanges (2020-2021) reports positive abnormal returns before the event turning negative from day +1 (https://thesis.eur.nl/pub/65625/Laucht_603384_Thesis.pdf). Coin Metrics finds the Coinbase effect is much smaller than Messari's headline (-1% to +14% from D-10 to D+10), so outlier-driven averages are a danger (https://cointelegraph.com/news/coinmetrics-finds-the-coinbase-effect-is-actually-pretty-lame). Theses are weak evidence; I did not read the full papers.
ideas.data: Kraken Futures instruments endpoint (verified; openingDate gives perp launch dates, 'tradeable' flag); Kraken spot AssetPairs (verified, no listing date, so snapshot daily and diff going forward); Binance announcements CMS list endpoint (verified returned 200: https://www.binance.com/bapi/composite/v1/public/cms/article/list/query?type=1&catalogId=48&pageNo=1&pageSize=3 , unofficial, may break); Kraken Futures charts for perp history; Binance data.binance.vision for Binance-listed tokens as a larger-sample proxy. History 2021-2026, a few hundred Binance events but only a few dozen with a Kraken perp.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures perps (short). Tokens without a perp cannot be shorted on Kraken: test on Binance perps for sample size, then restrict to the Kraken-tradeable subset for the paper run; say so honestly.
ideas.test: Design: Binance listing events 2021-01 to 2025-06 (use perps' first-day data from data.binance.vision), grid limited to 3 holding periods x 2 entry times = 6 trials. Control sealed: 2025-07 to 2026-11 events and all Kraken Futures openingDate events in that period. Pass if control net mean per trade > +2% after 0.15% round-trip cost and 0.5% slippage, median > 0, the top 3 winners are not responsible for more than 50% of the profit, and the Kraken-tradeable subset has >= 20 events. Evaluate the worst single gap (+40% squeeze) in drawdown.
ideas.expected: Honest: 0% to +6% per year net, highly variable. Event count on Kraken perps is small, so the test may be underpowered and inconclusive; the tail risk of one violent squeeze can erase a year. Max drawdown 10-20% on EUR 1,000 with 5% sizing.

ideas.name: Macro-release windows: pre-FOMC/CPI drift and post-event vol sale on BTC/ETH
ideas.rule: Variant A (directional, simple): go long PF_XBTUSD at 24 h before each scheduled FOMC decision (14:00 ET) and flatten 1 h before the release; 1x leverage, no stop. Variant B (only if A shows signal): after the release, fade the first 30-min move on CPI/FOMC when it exceeds 1.5x the 30-day average 30-min range, hold 4 h. Only one variant is frozen for the control.
ideas.rationale: Who pays: for pre-announcement drift in equities (Lucca-Moench), the premium is for bearing announcement-uncertainty risk, paid to those who hold risk before the event; with crypto, leveraged traders reduce open interest before FOMC and then re-lever after, which might leave a pre-event rebound and post-event reversal. It persists only if the structural deleveraging flows keep happening; the evidence for it in BTC is thin, so this is the weakest rationale of the three, and might be pure noise from a small sample (~60-70 FOMC meetings since 2019, ~90 CPI).
ideas.evidence: Media analyses of 2025-26 meetings show BTC often rising into FOMC and falling in the following 7 days, but 7-day returns range from +6.9% to -29.6% across 10 meetings, no published methodology (https://cointelegraph.com/news/short-the-dip-and-buy-the-rip-what-fomc-outcomes-reveal-about-bitcoin-price-action ; https://cryptoslate.com/bitcoin-traders-dump-coins-within-48-hours-of-fed-meetings-as-new-data-reveals-systematic-fomc-weakness/ , which itself admits FOMC meetings did not produce a clean repeatable downside over the longer sample). An NOVA Lisbon paper with 57 announcements (2018-2024) finds that unexpected hikes lead to negative BTC returns (https://run.unl.pt/server/api/core/bitstreams/a28b97c5-2eea-4448-96bb-db7526af22ed/content), but I did not see a pre-drift test. No peer-reviewed pre-FOMC drift result for crypto was found; treat the prior as low.
ideas.data: Kraken Futures 1h/5m candles back to 2022 (verified), Binance data.binance.vision 1m klines back to 2019 for BTC/ETH; FOMC dates scraped from federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm (verified 200); CPI dates from the BLS release schedule (bls.gov; the BLS API v2 endpoint responded 200, schedule is a public page). About 60-70 FOMC events 2019-2026: small sample, so only large effects can be detected.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures PF_XBTUSD and PF_ETHUSD. Costs about 0.05% taker per side, so ~0.10% per trade, negligible against any real drift. Fully executable on paper.
ideas.test: Design period 2019-2024 on Binance data for the long sample, then sealed control 2025-01 to 2026-11 on Kraken Futures prices (about 15 FOMC, 22 CPI). One pre-registered window per variant; at most 8 trials. Placebo: same-length windows before random non-event days of the same weekday/time. Pass if control net mean > +0.3% per FOMC trade with t-stat > 2 on the design period, sign positive in the control, and the placebo distribution does not give the same result (p < 0.05). With ~15 control events the control has low power, so a fail is only ruled out at the 0.3% level and a pass must be treated as provisional. If both fail, close the idea, no further tuning.
ideas.expected: Honest: roughly 0% to +2% per year on EUR 1,000 (about 8 trades/year of +0.2-0.5%). Not a source of 'quick profit'; mainly useful as a cheap, falsifiable check. Drawdown: a single FOMC day can move BTC +/-5%, so 1x position gives about 5% loss on a bad trade, ~8% yearly drawdown.

verdicts.name: Token-unlock dilution short, beta-hedged
verdicts.fatal_flaws: The data is the weak point. Unlock schedules are paid or scrape-only, and scraped schedules are revised after the fact, so they are not point-in-time. That makes lookahead and survivorship (dead tokens) likely. Few tokens have a Kraken PF_ perp, and many perps were listed only in 2024-25. So the 2022-2025 design period is thin on Kraken. Using Binance perps as a proxy means the test is not on the traded venue. Getting 40 or more control events from 2025-07 to 2026-11 on Kraken-listed tokens with an unlock of 3% or more is unlikely, so the sealed control would be underpowered. The decline starts about 30 days ahead, so a T-14 entry catches only the tail. The idea's own cited practitioner test of 59 Binance perps was not robust after costs. Holding 17 days with a BTC hedge adds funding and basis noise, plus small-cap squeeze risk with an 8% stop. Collecting clean data alone would take more than the one day allowed.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: None directly. Related only in being a short-bias event study on perps. It is not covered by v1-v5, the wick robot, carry or ETFs.
verdicts.cost_check: Costs are about 0.10% per side plus 0.10-0.20% slippage, so roughly 0.4-0.6% round trip, plus funding over 17 days. The claimed mean of -15% CAR over 60 days shrinks to maybe 3-5% over the 17-day window once the hedge is applied. That is probably still above costs on paper. But the claimed edge comes from a biased sample of 36-38 large events, and the broader test failed after costs. The gross edge is not clearly above realistic costs with the control threshold of +1.5% net.

verdicts.name: Post-listing fade on newly listed perps / announced tokens
verdicts.fatal_flaws: The executable sample is too small. Kraken lists perps late and only for established tokens, so by the time a PF_ perp opens the pop and the fade are already over. Tokens without a perp cannot be shorted, and a paper test that shorts spot assets is not executable on Kraken for EU retail. The Binance proxy is a different population (tiny new tokens, huge funding, thin books), and the result does not transfer. The require of 20 or more Kraken-tradeable control events from 2025-07 onward is unrealistic. The paper evidence is weak and outlier-driven (Coin Metrics rebuts the headline effect). The Binance CMS endpoint is unofficial and not archived with announcement timestamps. Squeeze tails (+40% gaps) dominate the P&L, and the 15% stop on 5% notional does not bind in gaps. The edge is also widely known and already arbitraged by funding. New perps often carry very negative or very positive funding, so the carry is unknown.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: Partial conceptual overlap with the v5 wick/reversal family (mean reversion after a spike). Otherwise untested. Also very close to the v1-v3 'new coin' spot ideas if any were run.
verdicts.cost_check: Costs are 0.15% round trip plus 0.5% slippage, probably 1% or more on new thin perps with funding. The mean net of +2% needed is plausible only if the effect is large. The effect depends on a few outliers. The gross edge does not clearly exceed costs after realistic slippage on tokens at their most volatile.

verdicts.name: Macro-release windows: pre-FOMC/CPI drift and post-event vol sale on BTC/ETH
verdicts.fatal_flaws: The test is statistically inconsistent. A BTC FOMC window has a standard deviation of about 3% per trade. With about 50 design events, a +0.3% mean gives t of roughly 0.7, so the t>2 requirement is unreachable unless the true effect is about 0.8% or more. With 15 control events, power is near zero, so the result will be inconclusive whatever happens. The rationale (Lucca-Moench) is an equity risk-premium effect with no crypto replication, and the idea admits the evidence is thin. Variant B (fade the first 30 minutes) is a second hypothesis, with dozens of window and threshold choices, which invites overfitting on about 60 samples. Only about 8 trades per year means at most +2% per year, which fails the 'quick profit' goal. There is real overlap with already-tested territory: short-horizon BTC directional timing found nothing robust in v4/v5, and event reversals resemble the wick rule.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: Partial. Timing and seasonality on BTC (v5 intraday seasonality) and reversal after a spike (v5 wick) both cover similar ground. The macro-calendar conditioning itself is new.
verdicts.cost_check: Costs are negligible (0.10% round trip), so costs are not the problem. The edge is unproven and the sample is too small to prove or kill it within the time budget. Expected gross edge per trade is within noise.

ideas.name: Open-interest washout reversal (hourly, slower cousin of the wick robot)
ideas.rule: On each liquid perp (BTC, ETH, SOL and others), compute the 4h change in Binance USDT-M open interest (5-min series) and the 4h price return. When OI falls more than a fixed percentile (e.g. bottom 5% of its trailing 90-day distribution) while price falls more than 1.5 sigma, go long the Kraken perp (1x to 2x) at the next bar open, exit after 6h or at an ATR stop. Mirror short only if a pre-declared symmetry test passes. The key pre-registered variant is the entry delay: run the same rule with 5, 15, 30 and 60 min of latency to see whether the edge survives the delay that killed the wick rule.
ideas.rationale: Forced sellers (liquidated leveraged longs, margin calls) pay a price concession to liquidity providers. The OI drop marks deleveraging that is already done, so the selling pressure is exhausted, and the rebound compensates whoever absorbs the flow. The edge persists because capital to catch falling knives is scarce and risk-limited (same logic as the BIS carry paper: arbitrage capital is scarce and gets hit by margin spikes). Risk: in a real trend crash, OI falls and price keeps falling, and v4/v5 results show regime dependence.
ideas.evidence: No peer-reviewed study of post-washout returns was found; I searched for one and did not find it. Adjacent evidence only: Schmeling, Schrimpf, Todorov, Crypto carry, BIS WP 1087 (https://www.bis.org/publ/work1087.htm) shows leverage and liquidation spikes drive crypto crashes and scarce arbitrage capital; Cheng et al., Liquidation, Leverage and Optimal Margin in Bitcoin Futures (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2102.04591) quantifies forced liquidations (about 3.5% of OI per day on BitMEX); arXiv 2607.27070 uses the same 5-min OI, long/short and taker-flow variables for cascade early warning. Giagkiozis and Said (Ledger, 2024) warn that exchange-reported OI is sometimes misquoted, so the OI series is a noisy input. The project's own result (wick reversal +37.6% over 121 days, but only with entry under 1 minute) is the closest internal evidence, and also a warning that slower entries may lose the effect.
ideas.data: Binance public data dump https://data.binance.vision/data/futures/um/daily/metrics/<SYMBOL>/<SYMBOL>-metrics-YYYY-MM-DD.zip (checked: BTCUSDT 2024-06-01 returns 200; 5-min open interest, top-trader and global long/short ratios, taker buy/sell ratio; coverage from about late 2020, older months may be missing per symbol, to verify). The REST endpoint fapi.binance.com/futures/data/openInterestHist (200 OK) only keeps about 30 days, so use it only for live paper feed. Prices: Kraken charts API https://futures.kraken.com/api/charts/v1/trade/PF_XBTUSD/1h (200 OK, also mark and spot tick types) or Binance klines in the same dump.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures perpetuals (PF_ symbols, up to 10x paper). Signal data comes from Binance, so the paper robot needs a live OI poll (Binance fapi, public, 5-min), which is free. Kraken's own OI is not available as history.
ideas.test: Design period Jan 2021 to Dec 2025 chosen as development, with at most 20 parameter trials (OI percentile, price threshold, holding time, stop) counted against the budget. Sealed control: 1 Jan 2026 to 27 Nov 2026, run once. Costs: 0.05% taker per side plus 0.05% slippage, funding included. Pass criteria: control net return above 0 after costs at entry delay of 15 min, profit factor above 1.3, at least 40 events in control, positive in at least 4 of 6 symbols, and the result not driven by the top 3 events. Kill rule: if the edge exists only at delay under 1 minute, report it as the same effect as the wick robot and stop.
ideas.expected: Honest prior is that this fails the delay test more often than not. If it works: roughly +5% to +20% per year on EUR 1,000 (EUR 50 to 200), with 20% to 30% drawdown at 2x because events cluster in crashes. Most likely outcome: near zero after costs at 15-min delay.

ideas.name: Dated-futures basis carry with term-structure gate (Kraken fixed-maturity vs spot)
ideas.rule: Each week, read Kraken Futures dated contracts (FF_XBTUSD_YYMMDD, FF_ETHUSD_YYMMDD) and compute annualised basis = (futures mark / spot index - 1) x 365 / days to expiry. If the best contract's net annualised basis (after 0.05% x 2 on the futures and 0.40% x 2 on the spot leg, or use a USD stablecoin/collateral leg to avoid spot taker fees) exceeds a hurdle of about 8% per year, hold long spot plus short dated future to expiry, locking the basis (convergence at expiry, no funding uncertainty). Otherwise stay in cash. Size the futures leg at under 2x with margin buffer of 30%+, to survive a squeeze.
ideas.rationale: Twist versus the funding carry already running: a dated future converges to spot by contract, so the return is known at entry and does not depend on future funding rates. Who pays: trend-chasing retail and leveraged longs who want long exposure without borrowing, and who pay a convenience yield (Schmeling et al.). Why it persists: arbitrage capital is scarce and the trade can be margin-called in crashes. The gate avoids carrying when the basis is thin: today FF_XBTUSD_270625 is about 4.3% above FF_XBTUSD_261204 over about 7 months (roughly 7% annualised), and Dec-26 is far lower, so right now the trade would barely clear costs, which is itself the honest finding.
ideas.evidence: Schmeling, Schrimpf, Todorov, Crypto carry, BIS Working Paper 1087 (Apr 2023, rev. Oct 2025), https://www.bis.org/publ/work1087.htm : carry can exceed 40% per year at times, is driven by convenience yield from small-investor trend chasing and limited arbitrage capital, and high carry predicts crashes (so the trade has negative skew). Published, but the large numbers come from 2020-2021; since ETF-era basis trades compressed carry. Not independently tested here.
ideas.data: Kraken Futures public API https://futures.kraken.com/derivatives/api/v3/tickers (200 OK, lists FF_XBTUSD_261204/261225/270326/270625 and ETH equivalents with mark, OI, volume) and charts API /api/charts/v1/{trade|mark|spot}/<symbol>/<resolution> (200 OK for PF_XBTUSD; history for expired FF_ contracts to be verified, fallback is Deribit public API https://www.deribit.com/api/v2/public/get_book_summary_by_currency?currency=BTC&kind=future, 200 OK, and get_tradingview_chart_data for expired contracts, to verify). Historical Binance dated futures (CM) are in data.binance.vision too.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures (dated FF_ contracts) plus Kraken spot, both in the arena broker. Caveat: dated-contract volume is small (e.g. XBT 261225 volumeQuote about 34k and ETH 270625 about 30), so paper fills are optimistic and real size is capped.
ideas.test: Build the basis time series from 2022 (when data exists) to Dec 2025 as design (only 3 to 5 parameters: hurdle, tenor, leverage cap, roll rule). Sealed control: Jan to Nov 2026, run once. Marks: daily mark-to-market including margin calls on the futures leg, and a stress test with a +30% spot move in 3 days. Pass: control net annualised return above spot EUR cash rate (about 2%) by at least 3 points with max margin utilisation under 60%, and no forced liquidation in the stress test. Note that the sample has very few independent episodes, so the pass is evidence of viability, not of statistical significance.
ideas.expected: About +3% to +8% per year net when the hurdle is met (EUR 30 to 80 on EUR 1,000), often nothing when the basis is thin. Drawdown small (under 5%) if margin is managed, but capital sits idle for much of the year. Do not expect more; the ceiling is the basis.

ideas.name: Perp premium dislocation fade (Kraken trade price vs spot index, 1-minute)
ideas.rule: On each Kraken PF_ perp, compute premium = (last trade or mark price / spot index - 1) at 1-minute resolution, and its z-score vs the trailing 7-day distribution. When z is above +3 (perp rich vs spot), short the perp; when below -3, go long, with a limit order at the touch (maker). Exit when z returns inside +/-0.5 or after 30 minutes. A second filter, to be decided before the test: skip when the premium moves together with a Binance one-minute return above 1% (a real move, not a dislocation).
ideas.rationale: Premium spikes beyond what funding explains reflect impatient, one-sided flow into a thin book; arbitrageurs (spot-versus-perp) and market makers pull it back to the index within minutes. The trader paid is the impatient taker. It persists because the arbitrage is capacity-limited and exchanges' own funding mechanism only corrects slowly. Honest risk: when spot itself leads (Binance moves first), a high perp premium is just the perp catching up, and fading it loses.
ideas.evidence: No direct paper found for Kraken. Related published evidence: Schmeling et al. (BIS WP 1087, https://www.bis.org/publ/work1087.htm) document excess volatility of futures versus spot and limits to arbitrage; Silantyev (2019, Digital Finance, https://link.springer.com/doi/10.1007/s42521-019-00007-w) shows trade-flow imbalance explains contemporaneous price moves on BitMEX; practitioner and thesis work (Erben 2023, Charles University) on Binance order book price impact. The predictive step (fading) is an untested hypothesis from this lens and the order-flow caveat applies: most flow-imbalance R-squared is contemporaneous, not forward-looking.
ideas.data: Kraken charts API https://futures.kraken.com/api/charts/v1/trade/PF_XBTUSD/1h and .../mark/... and .../spot/... all returned 200 with candles (the spot tick type is the index), so the premium can be built entirely from Kraken itself; verify that 1m resolution goes back far enough (suspected from 2022). Cross-check with Binance premiumIndexKlines 1m from https://data.binance.vision/data/futures/um/daily/premiumIndexKlines/BTCUSDT/1m/ (200 OK).
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures perpetuals. Needs maker fills at 1-minute latency, so it fits the existing 5-second robot infrastructure.
ideas.test: Design: Jan 2023 to Dec 2025 on 6 liquid perps, 15 trials maximum. Sealed control: Jan to Nov 2026. Model costs as taker 0.05% x2 plus slippage and a second scenario with maker entry at 0.02% and a 50% fill probability (missed fills counted as non-trades, with adverse selection: fills only if price trades through). Pass: net positive in control in both cost scenarios, profit factor above 1.25, at least 100 trades, and positive in at least 4 of 6 symbols. Kill: if gross edge per trade is below 0.12% before costs, stop immediately, since fees alone eat it.
ideas.expected: Most likely it fails on costs. Optimistic case: +5% to +15% per year on EUR 1,000 with 10% to 15% drawdown at 2x, but I would assign under 25% probability of passing control. Value is mainly as a cheap, fast falsification and as a possible filter for the wick robot.

verdicts.name: Open-interest washout reversal (hourly, slower cousin of the wick robot)
verdicts.fatal_flaws: Not fatal, but weak. (1) Power: a 5% OI percentile plus a -1.5 sigma 4h return gives only about 15-30 events per symbol per year, and they cluster in the same crash days across symbols. Pooled across 6 symbols the 40-event minimum in an 11-month control is barely met, and the events are not independent, so the 4-of-6-symbols criterion is nearly meaningless. (2) Overlap: OI collapse together with a sharp price drop is largely the same liquidation-cascade event as the wick rule, so a pass may be the wick effect re-measured. Add a mandatory check of what share of events coincide with wick-robot triggers, and a result computed after excluding those events. (3) OI comes from Binance and Kraken-perp price from another venue: a basis/latency mismatch the backtest hides. (4) Regime risk: in a real trend crash, OI falls and price keeps falling; v4 and v5 showed regime dependence. (5) The data dump snapshot timestamps must be checked so the 4h OI change uses only data available at decision time; otherwise there is lookahead. (6) Budget: 20 trials on a 4-parameter grid over 5 years of data is a loose multiple-testing guard.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: High partial overlap with the liquidation-wick reversal (v5; now a live 5-s robot and being rolled out to all liquid perps). Not identical: the horizon is 4h with 6h holds, and OI conditioning is new. Daily-scale mean reversion was tested in v1-v3 (no candidate) and 4h trend in v4, but 4h capitulation reversion with an OI filter was not. The pre-registered delay ladder (5/15/30/60 min) is a good kill criterion.
verdicts.cost_check: Round trip about 0.10% fee plus about 0.10% slippage, so about 0.2% in total, plus funding over 6h (small). Needs a gross edge above about 0.3% per trade, and 4h declines of 1.5 sigma on BTC are about 2%, so a 6h rebound of 0.5-1% is plausible but unproven. The cost threshold is passable in principle; the decisive risk is whether any edge remains after the 15-minute delay.
verdicts.fatal_flaws_summary_note: Keep only as a cheap falsification test. Run the wick-overlap and delay-ladder checks first; stop if the edge exists only at delay under 5 minutes.

verdicts.name: Dated-futures basis carry with term-structure gate (Kraken fixed-maturity vs spot)
verdicts.fatal_flaws: (1) The history needed for the test is probably not free: the Kraken charts API likely does not serve expired FF_ contracts, and Deribit expired-contract history is patchy, so a 2022-2025 design period with a gated basis series is unlikely within a day. (2) Statistically unfalsifiable: only a handful of independent expiry episodes, and the author admits it. A sealed control of Jan-Nov 2026 is 1-2 expiries. (3) Contract mismatch: Kraken FF_XBTUSD dated futures are inverse, coin-margined, USD-quoted, while the spot leg is EUR; this adds EUR/USD exposure and coin-margin convexity to the hedge, which the rule ignores. The arena's paper engine may not model inverse margin. (4) Today's measured basis (about 7% annualised, thinner further out) barely clears the hurdle, and capital efficiency is about half because the spot leg and margin buffer both tie up cash, so on EUR 1,000 the expected gain is EUR 20-40 per year, not distinguishable from the 2% cash rate. (5) Dated-contract volume is tiny (about 34k and about 30 quote units), so paper fills are fiction.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: Strong conceptual overlap with the cash-and-carry funding test now running (spot long plus perp short): the same economic engine (convenience yield paid by leveraged longs), same legs, fixed rather than floating carry. The only novelty is the locked basis, which does not justify a separate day of work.
verdicts.cost_check: Spot taker 0.40% twice is 0.8% over a holding period of roughly 6 months, so about 1.6% per year, plus 0.05% on the futures entry; expiry settlement is free. Net edge is about 7% - 1.7% = 5% on the notional, but about 2.5% on total capital after margin buffer, below or equal to the 2% cash hurdle plus 3 points required. Fails the pass criterion on its own numbers.
verdicts.fatal_flaws_summary_note: Sound economics, but below the noise floor and not testable here.

verdicts.name: Perp premium dislocation fade (Kraken trade price vs spot index, 1-minute)
verdicts.fatal_flaws: (1) Costs: Kraken perp premium z>3 versus the 7-day distribution usually corresponds to a few basis points (a few to 15 bps); the author's own kill rule needs a gross edge of at least 0.12% per trade, which most +3 sigma events will not reach. Premium reversion is also partly the trade price mean-reverting inside the bid-ask spread, i.e. bounce, which a taker cannot capture. (2) The maker variant has severe adverse selection: a limit order at the touch fills precisely when the dislocation is real and price keeps moving through; the fill model in the test ('price trades through') only partly fixes this and is optimistic with 1-minute candles. (3) Data: the 'mark' series is built from the index plus a funding-based premium, so mark versus spot is circular and not an independent signal; only trade versus spot is usable; 1-minute history depth and pagination on the Kraken charts API are unverified, and last-trade candles in thin periods give stale-price artefacts that look like dislocations. (4) Lookahead: 1-minute candles close-to-entry timing is easy to get wrong, and the entry is simulated at the same bar that defines the signal. (5) Edge already harvested: market makers and basis arbitrageurs at 1-minute granularity are the most competitive participants; retail with 5-second latency is the slow side.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: Overlaps the wick reversal (dislocation spikes are mostly the same events as liquidation wicks, where the edge only existed with entry under 1 minute) and the lead-lag/pairs family tested in v5 (cross-venue price leadership). The author admits the 'perp catches up' counter-scenario.
verdicts.cost_check: Taker round trip 0.10% plus slippage of about 0.03-0.05% each way, so about 0.15-0.2% per trade in total versus an expected gross reversion of a few basis points to about 0.1%. Fails. The maker scenario at 0.02% per side is better but suffers adverse selection and a 50% fill rate that is unsupported by evidence.
verdicts.fatal_flaws_summary_note: Likely a quick negative result; value only as a filter for the wick robot, which is a different, cheaper experiment than a standalone strategy.

ideas.name: Cross-sectional perp premium reversal (market-neutral, perps only)
ideas.rule: Every hour, for each liquid Kraken PF_ perp (24h volume above about 2M USD), compute premium = last trade / spot index - 1, standardised by its own 30-day std. Short the 3 perps with the highest z-score and long the 3 with the lowest (equal notional, beta-hedged with PF_XBTUSD), only if |z| > 2 and the raw premium is larger than the round-trip cost estimate. Exit when z crosses 0 or after 12 h. Funding accrues as a bonus, since high premium means longs pay shorts.
ideas.rationale: Perp premium is a mechanical anchor: retail leverage demand pushes the perp away from spot, and the funding mechanism and arbitrageurs pull it back. Who pays: impatient leveraged takers who cross the spread at a premium. The edge persists because spot-perp arbitrage on small caps needs capital and a spot leg that costs 0.4% taker on Kraken, so the premium can stay wide on mid-cap perps. It differs from the failed directional funding rule because the signal is the mark-vs-index gap, not the funding sign, and the book is dollar-neutral. Risk: it overlaps with the funding result, so the same overfit mode could reappear.
ideas.evidence: He, Manela, Ross, von Wachter, Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures (https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.06888): deviations from the no-arbitrage price are large in crypto, co-move across coins, shrink over time, implied arbitrage has high Sharpe ratios (no numbers on the abstract page I read). Gornall, Rinaldi, Xiao, Perpetual Futures and Basis Risk (preliminary, 2025): perp drawdowns mean-revert quickly (I only saw this via search summary, not the paper). Hyperliquid study (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.22839): hourly premium AR(1) about 0.72, half-life about 2 h (venue-specific, not Kraken). My own check today on Kraken 1-minute data, last 3 days: trade-vs-index deviation std is 1.8 bp for PF_XBTUSD, 4.0 bp for PF_SOLUSD, 5.4 bp for PF_DOGEUSD, with extremes of 20 to 35 bp on SOL and DOGE. Typical bid-ask on mid-caps is 5 to 20 bp, so only the tails clear costs.
ideas.data: Kraken Futures public charts API, verified live: https://futures.kraken.com/api/charts/v1/{trade|spot|mark}/{SYMBOL}/{1m|5m|1h}?from=&to= (about 2000 candles per call, paginate; 1h history for PF_XBTUSD goes back to March 2022). Funding: /derivatives/api/v3/historical-funding-rates?symbol=PF_XBTUSD (hourly, from late 2025 at least). Live premium/spread: /derivatives/api/v3/tickers (markPrice, indexPrice, bid, ask for 195 PF_ perps, 38 with more than 1M USD daily quote volume). Caveat: the chart 'spot' series is the Kraken index, so the 1h candle gap includes index construction noise; verify with the tickers snapshot logged every minute for a week.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures perps (EU retail eligible), leverage 2x to 3x only. Fees about 0.05% taker plus real spread.
ideas.test: Design on 1h data 2023-01 to 2026-06 (grid limited to about 12 trials: z threshold 1.5/2/2.5, hold 6/12/24 h, top-k 2/3/5). Seal the last 120 days (2026-07 to 2026-11) untouched. Costs: 5 bp fee per leg plus half the observed spread from a tickers snapshot, 2x on tail-liquidity coins. Pass: net of costs positive in at least 3 of 4 design years, control net return above 0 with at least 150 trades, results stable when slippage is doubled, and the PnL not explained by a BTC-beta or funding-only regression (alpha t-stat above 2). Kill if the edge only exists on coins with spread above 15 bp.
ideas.expected: Honest: EUR 0 to 60 per year on EUR 1,000 (0 to 6%), with realistic odds that it nets to zero after costs. Drawdown 5 to 10% with beta hedge; a single squeeze day on a small cap can cost 3 to 5% if stops are not hard-coded. Not a source of fast profit.

ideas.name: Stablecoin discount wick bids on Kraken (USDT/USD, USDC/USD, USDG, RLUSD, PYUSD, USDC/EUR, USDT/EUR)
ideas.rule: Keep a resting limit buy on each stablecoin pair at a discount level (grid 20, 30, 50 bp below 1.000 or below the FX-implied parity for the EUR pairs). On fill, post a limit sell at 1.0000 (or 5 bp below) and hold until filled or 10 days, then exit at market. Size per fill at most 25% of the portfolio, no more than 2 stablecoins at once, and a hard exit if any coin trades below 0.97 for 1 hour (depeg risk).
ideas.rationale: Who pays: panicking or forced sellers that dump into a thin book (liquidations, redemption jitter, bots hitting stale bids) and accept 20 to 400 bp below par. Why they keep paying: stablecoin books on a single venue are thin, arbitrage via mint/redeem is slow and has minimum sizes and fees (Lyons and Viswanath-Natraj show that arbitrage access drives peg half-life, from 6 days to 3 days after Tether's reforms). A small account can sit in the book at a size that never moves the price. Risk is a true depeg (UST, USDC March 2023), where the bid fills and never recovers; that is the premium you are being paid for.
ideas.evidence: Lyons and Viswanath-Natraj, What Keeps Stablecoins Stable (https://www.nber.org/papers/w27136, JIMF 2023): arbitrage spreads of 30 to 70 bp, deviation half-life 3 to 6 days, deviations halved after Tether's treasury access reform. My check on Kraken daily bars (720 days): USDT/USD daily low was more than 20 bp below par on 58 days and USDC/USD on 33 days; PYUSD/USD on 66 days; daily-low extremes of -480 bp (USDT) and -1,000 bp (PYUSD) are probably thin-book wicks. Triangular arbitrage inside Kraken is dead: on 720 one-minute bars, USDT/EUR x EUR/USD vs USDT/USD gap has mean -0.1 bp, std 0.6 bp, max 2 bp, so the discount is in the single-pair wicks, not between pairs. Caveat: part of that low data may be unfillable prints; the Kraken stablecoin/FX fee table (support article 360039299431, 'How do stablecoin/FX fees work?') applies a flat maker=taker fee on these pairs and I could not read the exact $0-tier number, check before running.
ideas.data: Kraken REST, verified live: /0/public/OHLC?pair=USDTUSD&interval=1440 (720 bars max), and /0/public/Trades?pair=USDTUSD&since=... (tick-level history, paginated, free) which is needed to confirm that a bid at level L would actually have been hit by real size, not just a one-lot print. Depth: /0/public/Depth?pair=USDTEUR (current USDT/EUR top-of-book shows about 300k units per level, so wicks need size). Also the EUR side: /0/public/OHLC?pair=EURUSD and USDTEUR.
ideas.venue: Kraken spot (USDT/USD, USDC/USD, USDG/USD, RLUSD, PYUSD; EUR pairs USDT/EUR, USDC/EUR, RLUSD/EUR). The arena must support resting limit orders and fill them only against real trade-tape volume, otherwise paper results will be optimistic. Holding USD stablecoins also carries EUR/USD exposure for a EUR portfolio, so prefer the EUR pairs or hedge with PF_EURUSD (that perp trades only about 20 USD of volume per day, so hedging is not realistic; accept the FX noise or cap hold time).
ideas.test: Reconstruct fills from the Trades tape 2024-2026-06: a bid at level L fills only if cumulative volume traded at or below L is at least 3x our size, with a 1-second queue-delay penalty. Count fills, time to recovery, net P&L after the stablecoin fee. Design on 2024-01 to 2026-03 for 3 levels x 3 holding caps (9 trials), seal the last 8 months. Pass: positive net on at least 15 fills in the design period with at least 80% recovering to within 10 bp of par inside 10 days, control positive, and loss on the single worst fill smaller than 4 gains. Honest limitation: the number of independent events is tiny and a depeg event can dominate; do not read this as a statistical proof, only as a plausibility check.
ideas.expected: Honest: EUR 20 to 50 per year on EUR 1,000 (2 to 5%), mostly idle capital. Capital sits in cash otherwise, so the drag is nil. Left-tail: a real depeg to 0.90 on a 25% position costs about 2.5% of the portfolio per event; drawdown is small in normal years. Capacity is tiny, so this is a diversifier, not the fast-profit engine requested.

ideas.name: Gold on Kraken Futures: PAXG/XAUT perp vs synthetic XAU perp spread reversion
ideas.rule: Trade the spread between PF_PAXGUSD (or PF_XAUTUSD), which tracks the tokenised-gold spot market, and PF_XAUUSD, which tracks the OTC gold index. Compute the log spread, subtract its rolling 30-day mean, and enter when the deviation exceeds 2 standard deviations (about 40 bp): long the cheap leg, short the rich leg in equal USD notional. Exit at 0.3 sigma or after 3 days. Add weekend rule: widen the entry threshold on Saturday and Sunday, when the OTC gold index is stale and the token market is price-discovering.
ideas.rationale: Two instruments referencing the same asset with different microstructure: PF_XAUUSD marks off an index of the OTC gold market, which closes at weekends, while PAXG and XAUT trade 24/7 against crypto liquidity and a structural discount from redemption friction and a custody fee. Who pays: token holders and perp traders who need immediate execution in a thin market (the PAXG perp trades only about 0.4M USD per day). The relative price should revert because redemption/OTC arbitrage bounds it, but the bound is wide (tens of bp) because arbitrageurs need large size and settlement time, so a small account can capture the fluctuations inside the band. Both legs are perps (0.05% fee), avoiding the 0.4% spot taker fee.
ideas.evidence: My check on the last 80 days of Kraken 1h data: PF_PAXGUSD / PF_XAUUSD log-spread mean -8 bp, std about 20 bp, lag-1 autocorrelation of the demeaned spread 0.80, lag-24h 0.66 (so slow reversion, half-life several days), 686 of 1,920 hours more than 20 bp from the mean; weekend std 18.5 bp vs weekday 20.0, so the weekend effect is NOT visible in this sample. Over 29 days PF_PAXGUSD vs spot PAXG/USD differed by only 5.8 bp std, so the perp follows spot well and the spread is real instrument-vs-instrument. Spot PAXG/USD, PAXG/EUR and XAUT/USD exist on Kraken (verified in AssetPairs). Theory support is only general (He et al., arXiv 2212.06888, on perp deviations; Makarov and Schoar, JFE 2020, https://mitsloan.mit.edu/node/38240, on arbitrage limits from segmentation) and I found no paper specifically on tokenised-gold basis, so the economic rationale is plausible but not published.
ideas.data: Kraken Futures charts API for PF_PAXGUSD, PF_XAUTUSD, PF_XAUUSD, PF_XAGUSD (1h and 5m, from early 2024 depending on listing date; check openingDate in /derivatives/api/v3/instruments) and hourly funding history via /derivatives/api/v3/historical-funding-rates. Cross-check for the true gold price: free daily LBMA/FRED-type gold series or spot XAU from any free FX/commodities feed (not verified, optional). The 'spot' kind of the charts API gives each perp's own index.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures perps (PF_PAXGUSD, PF_XAUTUSD, PF_XAUUSD all listed, tradeable, EU entities in platformsPermitted for PF_ crypto perps; confirm PF_XAUUSD eligibility for EU retail in the instruments metadata, since tradfi flag and marginSchedules differ). Same arena paper engine as the other perp robots.
ideas.test: Design on 2025-01 to 2026-05 data (about 8 trials: entry 1.5/2/2.5 sigma, exit 0/0.3, max hold 3/5 days), costs = 5 bp per leg per side (4 fills) plus half of live spread (log tickers every minute for a week to calibrate; PAXG perp spread is wider than BTC) plus funding differential. Seal 2026-06 to 2026-11. Pass: net positive in at least 70% of calendar months in design, at least 30 round trips, control net positive, and result survives doubling the spread. Kill if round-trip cost is above 60% of the average captured deviation (a quick arithmetic check on the data before any backtest: at about 25 to 30 bp round-trip cost and 2-sigma entries of 40 bp, the margin is only 10 to 15 bp per trade, so this may die at step one).
ideas.expected: Honest: roughly EUR 0 to 40 per year (0 to 4%) on EUR 1,000 and a decent chance of zero after real spreads. Drawdown 2 to 4% (hedged, but a gold-token-specific shock like a custody or redemption scare can push the spread 100 bp the wrong way). It is mainly a low-correlation, low-return sleeve, and a cheap way to learn whether any perp relative-value signal survives costs.

verdicts.name: Cross-sectional perp premium reversal (market-neutral, perps only)
verdicts.fatal_flaws: The signal is last trade versus the index. That gap includes bid-ask bounce and index-construction noise, so most of the measured mean reversion cannot be traded. It would show up in a backtest on mid or last-trade prices and vanish when you cross the spread. Premium std is 4-5 bp on mid-caps, so a |z|>2 entry is about 10 bp, and the reversion you can capture is perhaps half of that. A 6-leg book has 12 fills per cycle plus a BTC hedge leg. On the mid-caps where premiums are widest, the 5-20 bp spreads and the thin books (low-volume mid-cap perps) kill it. The candle 'last' and 'spot' closes are not simultaneous snapshots, which adds a timestamp-alignment lookahead risk. Hourly data cannot resolve a half-life of about 2 h. The 'beta hedge' adds cost and noise. It is also a close cousin of the funding signal that collapsed in the sealed control, since funding is a function of the premium. The stated 12-trial grid is tidy, but the true multiplicity (coins x thresholds x hedge choices) is larger.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: Heavy overlap with the v5 directional funding rule (funding is the smoothed premium) and with cross-sectional lead-lag/pairs on perps. The premium is a different measurement but the same underlying anchor. Partial overlap with the running cash-and-carry and cross-venue funding-spread work.
verdicts.cost_check: Fails. Expected gross edge is roughly 5-10 bp per leg on tail entries. Realistic round-trip cost is about 10 bp in fees plus 10-40 bp in spread and slippage per leg on mid-caps. Gross edge is below cost, and the author's own caveat ('only the tails clear costs') confirms it.

verdicts.name: Stablecoin discount wick bids on Kraken (USDT/USD, USDC/USD, USDG, RLUSD, PYUSD, USDC/EUR, USDT/EUR)
verdicts.fatal_flaws: This is the only one of the three worth a day of work, and it is conditional. (1) Fee: the Kraken stablecoin/FX flat fee has not been read. If it is 0.10-0.20% per side, a 20-30 bp bid is wiped out. Check the fee first and drop to the 50 bp level or maker-only if so. (2) Fill realism: daily-low wicks of -480 bp and -1,000 bp are almost certainly tiny prints. The tape-volume test (3x size, queue delay) is the right guard, but it needs a paper engine that fills resting limits only against real tape. (3) Sample size: a handful of independent events, so it is a plausibility check and not proof. A true depeg (USDC March 2023 style) dominates the tail. (4) USD stablecoin legs add EUR/USD noise (prefer the EUR pairs) and the order book is dominated by market makers. (5) Capacity is tiny, and the return is about 2-5% per year at best, so it does not meet the 'fast profit' goal. It is a diversifier.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: None. It is not a trend, funding or wick-reversal rule. It resembles the liquidation-wick reversal only in spirit: passive liquidity provision against forced sellers, in a different asset class with a hard par anchor. Do not count it as a new directional edge.
verdicts.cost_check: Conditional. If the stablecoin pair fee is 0.02-0.10%, a 30-50 bp discount with recovery to par gives roughly 20-45 bp net per fill, which clears costs. At 0.20% per side the 20 bp level is dead. Verify the fee table before building. No spread is paid, because the order rests, but adverse selection is real.

verdicts.name: Gold on Kraken Futures: PAXG/XAUT perp vs synthetic XAU perp spread reversion
verdicts.fatal_flaws: The author's own arithmetic already kills it. Four fills at about 5 bp is 20 bp, plus half-spreads on a PAXG perp trading about 0.4M USD per day (likely 5-15 bp per leg), plus a funding differential. Round-trip cost is about 30-60 bp against a capturable move of about 34 bp (2 sigma to 0.3 sigma at 20 bp std). Only 80 days of history, with perp listings from 2024 at best, gives a tiny design sample with a possible structural mean shift (-8 bp mean). There is no weekend effect in the data, so that rule has no support. PF_XAUUSD and tradfi-linked perps may not be open to EU retail. A tokenised-gold shock (custody, redemption) gives fat-tail risk with no hedge. The 70% positive months pass test is statistically meaningless with 17 months. Test multiplicity is small but the effective sample is a few dozen round trips.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: No direct overlap with a tested rule. Conceptually it belongs to the pairs/relative-value family that failed in v5 (cross-sectional lead-lag/pairs) and the ETF cross-asset work that found no edge after costs.
verdicts.cost_check: Fails. Net margin per trade is about zero or negative once real spreads on the thin gold-token perps are included.

ideas.name: Adverse-event short: hacks/exploits and regulatory enforcement, classified by an LLM, executed on Kraken perps
ideas.rule: For each timestamped adverse event (protocol exploit, SEC/regulator action naming a token, exchange withdrawal halt), an LLM reads the source text with a frozen prompt and outputs: affected tradeable ticker, severity (funds lost vs TVL/market cap), and whether the loss is already contained. Open a short on the Kraken PF_ perp of the affected token (or of the native chain token) at the next 5-minute bar after the article timestamp plus a 5-minute lag, only if severity is above a threshold fixed before the test; hold 3 to 7 days or stop at +8%, size at 1/10 of equity per event, leverage at most 2x.
ideas.rationale: Who pays: holders of the token who are slow to sell, and liquidity providers/market makers who widen spreads only after the fact. Drift persists because spot sellers face frictions (withdrawals, unlocking, tax and custody decisions), many holders are retail and shorting alt tokens is hard on most venues. The LLM's edge is not speed but disentangling which hacks are material (a 2M exploit on a 5B token is noise; a bridge hack on a chain's collateral is not) and mapping the event to the correct ticker from free text, which regex cannot do. Weak points: most hacks hit tokens with no Kraken perp (195 PF_ perps are tradeable today), so the event count may be small (expect 30 to 80 usable events over 2021-2026), and the first minutes carry most of the move, so the test must show the drift survives a 5-minute lag.
ideas.evidence: Event study of SEC actions on crypto assets reports about -12% over one week persisting for a month (summarised in the SEC CTF input document https://www.sec.gov/file/ctf-input-arte-2025-02-19). Ripple/SEC delisting episode is the best-known case. No peer-reviewed study of LLM-classified hack announcements found; for hacks, evidence is mostly industry commentary, so this must be treated as unproven. LLM text-to-return papers exist but mostly report accuracy, not net-of-cost returns (e.g. https://arxiv.org/html/2502.14897v2, https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19349v3), so I would not rely on them.
ideas.data: DefiLlama hacks endpoint verified live and free: https://api.llama.fi/hacks returns 1378 incidents back to 2015 with date, name, amount, chain, classification, technique, source URL and description (no key). Kraken Futures instruments endpoint verified: https://futures.kraken.com/derivatives/api/v3/instruments (195 tradeable PF_ contracts). Kraken historical spot and OHLC verified: https://api.kraken.com/0/public/AssetPairs. Free timestamped text: GDELT DOC 2.0 (https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc, verified reachable but rate limited to 1 request per 5 seconds, history since 2017), plus the article URLs in the hacks table; for regulatory actions use SEC litigation release pages and Wayback timestamps. Caveat: DefiLlama dates are day-level, so the true intraday timestamp must be recovered from the linked source or GDELT; events without a recoverable timestamp are dropped, not guessed.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures perps (PF_ symbols) for tokens that have one; Kraken spot EUR pairs cannot be shorted without margin, so perps only. Costs: about 0.05% taker per side plus 0.1 to 0.3% slippage on mid-cap alts, plus funding (usually small when shorting in a bull market, it can be received or paid).
ideas.test: Design period: events 2021-01 to 2024-06; control sealed: 2024-07 to 2026-11, never inspected until the prompt, threshold and horizon are frozen. Controls: (a) same entry rule on random dates for the same tickers (placebo), (b) same rule on the matched tokens with no event, (c) market beta hedge by comparing with a short of BTC perp over the same window. Look-ahead guard: the LLM sees only text published before the entry timestamp, and use a model with training cutoff-aware prompts (strip names of outcomes; a model that has memorised 2022 hacks leaks the future, so keep the design period for tuning and weigh the control, which is later than the model's knowledge, most). Pass if, in the control, the mean net return per event after costs and a 5-minute lag is above +1.5%, the hit rate above 55%, at least 20 events, and a bootstrap 90% interval over events excludes zero, and the placebo mean is near zero. Kill immediately if the edge exists only when entering within 1 minute (as with the wick rule).
ideas.expected: Honest: about +3% to +8% per year net on EUR 1,000 with a small number of trades (perhaps 10 to 20 per year), with a wide interval that likely includes zero; a single short squeeze on a rebound can cost 8% of the position in a day. Max drawdown 5 to 10% of equity. Likely outcome after the sealed control: marginal or inconclusive because of the small sample; the main value is that the test is cheap and informative.

ideas.name: Exchange delisting and monitoring-tag announcements: short the afflicted token after the announcement (Kraken perp or spot sell-side avoidance)
ideas.rule: Scrape timestamped announcements from Binance (delisting, monitoring tag, and removal of margin pairs), Coinbase and Kraken (asset removals). The LLM extracts the token, the effective date, the stated reason (regulatory, low liquidity, security, voluntary) and whether it is a full delisting or only a pair. On a full delisting by a top-3 venue with a reason other than voluntary, short the Kraken perp from the next 5-minute bar after the announcement lag, close on the effective date minus 1 day or after 7 days, whichever is first; skip tokens without a Kraken perp or with an announced price rebound catalyst.
ideas.rationale: Who pays: holders forced out of positions (funds with venue-limited custody, leveraged longs liquidated when margin pairs are removed, retail sellers who learn late) and market makers who withdraw liquidity. The drift is plausible since the loss of liquidity and of the largest order books is a permanent structural downgrade, and a short seller cannot easily arbitrage it away on the small alts affected. The LLM's value: the notices are unstructured (tag vs delisting vs pair removal, different reasons), the effective dates and affected pairs are buried in text, and a fixed regex breaks between exchange templates. Weak points: the first reaction is immediate and may be most of the move; Binance announcement timestamps are second-level but the page is dynamic; and many delisted tokens have no Kraken perp, shrinking the sample to major names (event count perhaps 20 to 60 on the Kraken perp universe).
ideas.evidence: Li, Luo, Wang, Wei find positive short-run abnormal returns around listings, larger on Coinbase than Binance (https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.AFT.2025.11), and an event study on 390 cross-listings (2020-2021) shows positive run-up before and negative returns from day one after listing (https://thesis.eur.nl/pub/59675/Final-Draft.pdf); these concern listings, not delistings. I did not find a peer-reviewed delisting event study, so the symmetry (negative drift after delisting) is my hypothesis, not published evidence. Practitioner read: the move concentrates at announcement and fades once trading starts (https://www.thetie.io/insights/what-does-an-exchange-listing-actually-deliver-in-2026).
ideas.data: Binance announcements are available through the unofficial but public CMS endpoint https://www.binance.com/bapi/composite/v1/public/cms/article/list/query (catalogId 161 for delistings) with release dates in ms; the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx) covers older pages. I did not verify the Binance endpoint in this session (it is geo-restricted in some regions and may need a proxy), so treat it as to be confirmed. Kraken Futures price history verified at https://futures.kraken.com/derivatives/api/v3/instruments (195 PF_ perps); Kraken public spot OHLC verified at https://api.kraken.com/0/public/AssetPairs. Free and ready. Binance and Coinbase minute data from their public klines endpoints for the abnormal-return measurement.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures perps for the short; tokens without a Kraken perp are untestable here, so the sample is limited to liquid names. Costs: 0.05% taker per side, 0.1 to 0.3% slippage, funding paid or received over 1 to 7 days.
ideas.test: Design 2021-01 to 2024-06 for choosing the horizon (1, 3, 7 days) and the reason filter; sealed control 2024-07 to 2026-11. Compute the cumulative abnormal return versus a BTC/ETH beta model estimated on the 60 days before the announcement, at the lag of 5 minutes, 30 minutes and 4 hours after the announcement, to show how fast the edge vanishes. Placebo: pairs removals and voluntary delistings (should show no drift). Pass if the control mean net CAR at the 30-minute lag exceeds +2%, with at least 15 events and a positive bootstrap lower bound at 80%; if the edge is only at lag 5 minutes or less, reject, as an arena robot cannot capture it.
ideas.expected: Honest: +2% to +6% per year on EUR 1,000, with probably fewer than 10 trades a year; drawdown 5 to 8% from rebounds on pump-and-squeeze delisting names. The most likely failure is that the move is instantaneous and the 30-minute lag shows nothing. Value is mostly as a negative-result test with a clean design.

ideas.name: LLM-structured token unlock calendar: short the perp into large cliff unlocks, classified by recipient and overhang
ideas.rule: Build the calendar from governance documents, tokenomics pages and vesting contracts (LLM extracts: date, amount, recipient class such as team, investors, ecosystem, and whether it is a cliff or linear, plus whether the stated supply is circulating or total). Select only cliff unlocks above 2% of circulating supply going to team or investors on tokens with a Kraken PF_ perp. Open a short at 10 days before the unlock and close at 1 day after, 1/10 of equity per position at most 2x, skip if funding is below -0.05% per 8 hours (crowded short).
ideas.rationale: Who pays: recipients and their market makers hedge or sell ahead of the unlock, and retail longs keep buying on narrative. The drift persists because the unlocks are public yet disliked as a topic, since shorting alts is costly and many holders do not model dilution; the pre-event drift is an expensive-to-arbitrage supply pressure. The LLM's role is structured extraction, not prediction: schedules are inconsistent across docs (circulating vs total supply, cliff vs linear, who receives). Honest caveats: this is the most crowded of the three because unlocks are widely tracked, and the premium may already be priced in. Also a naive screen mixes beta, since the sample is mostly bear-market altcoins in 2022-2023.
ideas.evidence: Keyrock study of over 16,000 unlocks: about 90% show negative price pressure and declines begin about 30 days before (https://keyrock.com/from-locked-to-liquidity-what-16000-token-unlocks-teach-us/); this is a market maker report, not peer reviewed, and does not control for the market. Tokenomist reports a median -14.7% in the month before (n=164, correlational, https://tokenomist.ai/learn/glossary-term/unlock-price-impact). Contradicting: a Crypto Briefing report of about 600 events finds prices rising around most unlocks (https://cryptobriefing.com/tokens-rise-34-average-private-investors), and CryptoRank's 50-alt sample is mixed (https://cryptorank.io/insights/analytics/how-have-token-unlocks-affected-crypto-prices). The evidence is mixed and conflicts, which is a reason to demand the sealed control.
ideas.data: Hard part: free historical unlock data. DefiLlama's emissions endpoint is paywalled (https://api.llama.fi/emissions returned HTTP 402 in this session), Tokenomist has a paid API, so the free route is to extract schedules from project docs, Messari/CoinGecko-free pages and archived pages, which is where the LLM does real work and why this is a 2-3 day job rather than 1. Prices: Kraken Futures history (195 PF_ perps verified, https://futures.kraken.com/derivatives/api/v3/instruments) and Kraken spot OHLC (https://api.kraken.com/0/public/AssetPairs). If a complete event list cannot be built in a day, reduce to the 20 largest tokens.
ideas.venue: Kraken Futures perps. Costs: 0.05% per side plus 0.1-0.3% slippage, funding for 11 days (usually small, but can be -0.1% per day on crowded shorts, which the funding filter is meant to avoid).
ideas.test: Design 2022-01 to 2024-06 to fix the size threshold, window (T-10 to T+1) and recipient filter; sealed control 2024-07 to 2026-11. Benchmark every position against a beta-matched short of BTC and ETH plus a placebo with random dates on the same token, since a bear market flatters any short. Pass if the control shows mean beta-adjusted net return per event above +2%, at least 25 events and positive in at least 3 of 4 control quarters. Reject if the edge is in the design period only (likely, given the conflict in the literature).
ideas.expected: Honest: 0% to +5% per year net on EUR 1,000 after beta adjustment, with a real chance of negative. Absolute return will look better in a falling market but that is beta, not edge. Drawdown 8 to 15% because of squeezes on thin alts. This is the weakest of the three on novelty (crowded) but the best documented, so it is mainly a check of whether the published effect survives costs and a sealed control.

verdicts.name: Adverse-event short: hacks/exploits and regulatory enforcement, classified by an LLM, executed on Kraken perps
verdicts.fatal_flaws: 1) The sealed control cannot reach the required 20 usable events. Few hacked tokens have a Kraken PF_ perp, DefiLlama dates are day-level, and events without a recoverable intraday timestamp are dropped. The author's own estimate is 30-80 events over 5 years, so the 2024-07 to 2026-11 window likely holds under 15. 2) LLM leakage: a model with a cutoff around mid-2026 has memorised the outcomes of the entire control period, so the control is not clean for an LLM classifier. The prompt-stripping idea does not fix this. 3) Hack news spreads within minutes, and the sample is dominated by the first-minute move. This is the same failure mode as the wick rule (edge only under 1 minute of latency). 4) The 3-7 day drift is confounded by market beta and by rebounds. 5) The SEC -12% evidence concerns 2023 enforcement against a few named tokens and is not a hack-drift result. 6) An LLM adds little over a simple severity ratio (amount lost / market cap), which needs no LLM.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: No direct overlap. The nearest are the liquidation-wick reversal (a short-latency event reaction) and the LLM-as-trader results (LLMs reading text have not beaten simple engines). The LLM here is only an extractor, so the overlap is partial.
verdicts.cost_check: Costs are 0.10% in fees plus 0.2-0.6% in slippage on a round trip, about 0.5-0.7% in total. The claimed edge of 1.5-3% per event clears this on paper, but with fewer than 15 events the confidence interval swamps it and one squeeze costs 8%. The edge net of costs is not demonstrable with this sample.

verdicts.name: Exchange delisting and monitoring-tag announcements: short the afflicted token after the announcement (Kraken perp or spot sell-side avoidance)
verdicts.fatal_flaws: 1) Universe mismatch. Kraken Futures lists only liquid, mostly large-cap perps, while Binance, Coinbase and Kraken delist and tag small illiquid tokens that rarely have a PF_ perp. The overlap is likely a handful of events (single digits in 2024-2026), well under the required 15. 2) The Binance CMS endpoint is unverified and geo-restricted, and the Wayback route is slow and incomplete, so the data is not free within a day. 3) The reaction is immediate. The author concedes the likely failure (a 30-minute lag shows nothing), and the pass criterion requires a +2% net abnormal return at a 30-minute lag. 4) No published delisting evidence exists. The cited evidence concerns listings. 5) Delisted tokens are often borrow-constrained or move in spikes, so the paper fills would not be realistic.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: No direct overlap. It shares the sub-minute event-reaction failure mode with the wick rule, and the event-driven LLM-extraction design resembles the hack idea.
verdicts.cost_check: Costs of about 0.5-1.0% round trip are affordable if the edge were real, but on thin tokens that do have perps the slippage can be 1% or more. The expected gross edge after a 30-minute lag is probably near zero, so costs consume what is left.

verdicts.name: LLM-structured token unlock calendar: short the perp into large cliff unlocks, classified by recipient and overhang
verdicts.fatal_flaws: 1) Historical unlock data is not free. DefiLlama emissions returned 402 and Tokenomist is paid. Rebuilding schedules from project docs is a 2-3 day job, so it fails the one-day constraint. 2) Point-in-time lookahead: schedules and circulating-supply figures get revised, and reconstructing them from archived docs risks using later knowledge. 3) The effect is the most crowded of the three, and the evidence is mixed (Keyrock and Tokenomist vs Crypto Briefing and CryptoRank). A short from T-10 to T+1 on tokens such as ARB, APT, SUI or OP is largely beta, and alt perps carry high squeeze risk. 4) The LLM is only an extractor of a deterministic calendar, so the novelty is low. 5) Funding on crowded alt shorts over 11 days can be sizeable.
verdicts.already_tested_overlap: No direct overlap with tested ideas. It is a bearish alt-token bias that a beta-adjusted test would likely strip. It is also partially related to the earlier directional-funding result, which was overfit and collapsed in control.
verdicts.cost_check: Round-trip costs of 0.5-0.8% plus funding of 0.2-1% over the hold total roughly 1-2%. The author's expected net edge of 0-5% per year, before a beta adjustment that probably removes most of it, does not clearly clear this.
